newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Short bonds outperform.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Short bonds outperform.

text.p: Australian three year bonds outperformed other dollar-bloc bonds on Wednesday, but the long end was unable to follow its lead, seeing the curve at its steepest level since mid July.
The local market was unable to shake off bearish sentiment surrounding U.S. Treasuries, with long dated bonds heaviest, ahead of Thursday's key labour force data.
Despite pulling back from their record highs last week, long bionds have still managed to improve slightly in spread terms over the first three days of this week.
"We're still outperforming the U.S. at the moment, and I can't see it crumbling down at the moment," one trader said.

Local fundamentals of low inflation, sluggish growth and a stalled labour market have supported the bond market in recent weeks and will keep the market looking for a sixth interest rate cut in coming months, traders said.

The modest growth outlook was reinforced by Wednesday's National Australia Bank business survey showing a deterioration in business conditions for July and an inability of firms to pass on price increases.
Thursday's labour force data was also expected to show little change in the labour market, with employment expected to rise by 25,000, with the unemployment rate edging up to 8.6 percent.
The weakness in the long end, which lost six points on the day, saw the yield curve continue its recent steepening trend.
The curve has steepened by about 15 points this week and is now at its steepest since July 15.
